lesson.text: Quick memory: what is an algorithm? (A list of clear steps in the right order.) Today you give the robot its steps.
A program is an algorithm written for a computer or a robot. Its steps run one after another, in order: a sequence. This robot faces right, so FORWARD 3 takes it three squares right.
FORWARD 3 is short for FORWARD, FORWARD, FORWARD. When you write the program, tap FORWARD three times.
A turn does not move the robot: it only changes the way it faces. TURN RIGHT, then FORWARD, moves it one square to its right.
Plan it: put your finger on the robot. Which way does it face? Count the squares to the flag, and turn when your finger has to turn.
There is often more than one right program. The shortest one uses the fewest steps.
Test your program: run it one step at a time. If the robot misses the flag, change one step and test again.
Try it in the world: mark a start block and a finish block. Write a program like “FORWARD 5, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD 3” and ask a friend to walk it exactly.

exercises.prompt: Which program takes the robot to the flag?
exercises.hint: Put your finger on the robot and follow each program one step at a time. A turn does not move it.
exercises.explain: FORWARD 4: the robot faces right, and four squares forward take it to the flag.

choices: moves the robot one square the way it faces
moves the robot to the flag at once
moves the robot one square to the left
exercises.explain: FORWARD moves the robot one square, the way it faces.

exercises.prompt: TURN LEFT moves the robot one square to the left.
exercises.hint: Does a turn move the robot to a new square?
exercises.explain: False: TURN LEFT only turns the robot a quarter turn where it stands. It needs FORWARD to move.

exercises.prompt: In a program, the steps run one after another, in order.
exercises.explain: True: a program's steps run in order, one after another. That is a sequence.

exercises.prompt: Write a program that takes the robot to the flag.
exercises.hint: First check which way the robot faces. Point that way, then plan one square at a time: a turn does not move it.

exercises.prompt: Which program takes the robot to the flag?
exercises.hint: Put your finger on the robot and follow each program one step at a time. A turn does not move it.
exercises.explain: FORWARD 2, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD 3: two squares up, a quarter turn right, three squares right.

exercises.prompt: The robot faces left. Which program takes it to the flag?
exercises.hint: Put your finger on the robot and follow each program one step at a time. A turn does not move it.
exercises.explain: FORWARD 3 takes it to the left side, TURN RIGHT points it up, and FORWARD 3 takes it to the flag.

exercises.prompt: How many FORWARD steps are in this program: FORWARD 2, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 3, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD?
exercises.hint: Add up the FORWARDs only. Turns do not move the robot.
exercises.explain: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 FORWARD steps. The turns don't count.

exercises.prompt: Write a program that takes the robot to the flag.
exercises.hint: First check which way the robot faces. Point that way, then plan one square at a time: a turn does not move it.
exercises.explain: One program that works: FORWARD 2, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD 3.

exercises.prompt: What does TURN RIGHT then TURN RIGHT do?
exercises.hint: Two quarter turns make how much of a whole turn?
choices: turns the robot to face the other way
moves it back to the start
exercises.explain: Two quarter turns make a half turn, so the robot faces the other way. It does not move.

exercises.prompt: Write a program that takes the robot to the flag. Go round the wall!
exercises.hint: First check which way the robot faces. Point that way, then plan one square at a time: a turn does not move it.
exercises.explain: One program that works: FORWARD, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 4, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD 3.

exercises.prompt: Write the shortest program that picks up the gem and then reaches the flag.
exercises.hint: First check which way the robot faces. Point that way, then plan one square at a time: a turn does not move it.
exercises.explain: One program that works: FORWARD 3, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 3.

exercises.prompt: Which program does the same as FORWARD, FORWARD, FORWARD, FORWARD?
exercises.explain: Four FORWARDs in a row can be written FORWARD 4.

exercises.prompt: TURN LEFT, TURN LEFT, TURN LEFT faces the robot the same way as one TURN RIGHT.
exercises.hint: Count the quarter turns. How many make a whole turn?
exercises.explain: True: three quarter turns to the left end the same way as one quarter turn to the right.

exercises.prompt: The robot runs FORWARD 3, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 2, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 3. How many squares does it move altogether?
exercises.hint: Turns don't move it. Add up the FORWARDs.
exercises.explain: 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 squares. The two turns don't move the robot.
